intent: Unify BE GOOD’s completed communication workflow into one Hebrew RTL tool named תקשורת מקדמת חוסן חברתי / Communication for Social Resilience, preserving an easy tab-only single-message mode and adding explicit lossless conversion into privately persisted ongoing communication. Both modes share the same versioned AI engine and eighteen principles; preserve eligible writer access, original source/draft/model/version provenance, independent optional research consent, and production deployment restrictions.

findings.suggested_fix: Do not use revision magnitude alone to accept a replayed transient document. Pin and compare the submitted document/proof or a local document generation, preserving the current document when another operation has replaced that base, including at equal revision. For the pending-conversion path, when no convert request was sent and subsequent work superseded its singleEdit base, discard that pre-conversion operation and start conversion from the current signed document and pending edits; retain exact destination/request replay once convert has been sent. Add the lost-pre-conversion-edit, equal-revision second-edit scenario to the UI tests.
findings.title: Conversion replay can erase an equal-revision manual edit
findings.why_it_matters: A user can lose a manually recorded draft after retrying conversion. If the pre-conversion singleEdit response is lost, the user can record a different edit from the still-visible base; both stateless signed results then have the same revision. Replaying the pinned conversion treats its older result as current, replaces the newer draft and proof, and converts the older text, leaving the later edit absent from both tab history and the saved conversation.
findings.validation_reason: At e443587 on Node v20.19.1, the actual UI VM and signed handler with an in-memory authorized staff store reproduced the reachable sequence of losing conversion's singleEdit(B) response, recording C from the still-visible revision-1 base, and retrying conversion: communication-continuity-ui.js:175-178 accepts replayed B at equal revision 2, leaving both the transient and saved document without C and no pending edit, behavior introduced by the new single-mode path.

findings.title: Corrected conversion keeps resubmitting rejected input
findings.why_it_matters: A user who receives a definitive input-limit rejection cannot correct the fields and convert the document afterward: every subsequent conversion submits the rejected snapshot again. For example, a 12,001-character optional instruction produces STORAGE_LIMIT; replacing it with a short instruction still submits 12,001 characters because the operation remains pinned once its convert body exists. Pinning is needed after an uncertain response, but a first, confirmed pre-commit validation rejection should allow a fresh corrected conversion.
findings.validation_reason: At e443587 on Node v20.19.1, the actual UI VM and handler reproduced a first conversion with a 12001-character instruction returning 413 STORAGE_LIMIT before any write and a corrected instruction still resubmitting length 12001 and returning 413, because the newly added communication-continuity-ui.js:230,249,275 retains the rejected operation and its cached body.

findings.title: Single JSON export drops pending sources and materials
findings.why_it_matters: After generating a draft, a user can change the source instruction or successfully upload another material, then export JSON while generation/conversion is unavailable. That backup silently excludes the changed composer fields and newly extracted material because it serializes only the last signed document and draft edits. Closing the tab then permanently loses those pending sources despite the UI presenting JSON as a full source/material archive. Capturing current input in separately labelled export-only fields preserves this offline recovery path without changing signed provenance.
findings.validation_reason: At e443587 on Node v20.19.1, changing the composer after generation and successfully uploading a signed TXT through the actual UI and handler produced a JSON export Blob containing none of the pending source, instruction, or material text, confirming that the new exportSingle call at communication-continuity-ui.js:704 snapshots only the old signed document and draft edits despite the complete-archive promise at :151 and tab-only storage contract R2.

findings.title: Exclude workspace instructions from single-mode demo documents
findings.why_it_matters: The single-mode demo saves the entire result workspace, so its example document contains JSON/export instructions, the conversion notice and the expanded system-version panel alongside the message. These remain visible when the administrator previews the product and when that example is published to the library, violating the written requirement that demo documents contain the edited product without screen instructions. Building the single-mode capture from the current draft text, as the normal single PDF export already does, makes the example match the delivered message.

findings.title: Image material guard rejects faithful quotations about emotions
findings.why_it_matters: A readable image containing text such as 'הוא מרגיש שמחה.' cannot be accepted as single-mode material even when the model transcribes that text exactly. The new attribution guard scans the combined verbatim source text and visual description, so it treats a quotation in a poem or message as an invented emotional claim, retries, and returns AI_OUTPUT_INVALID. This obstructs the preserved poem/image use case and can encourage the repair response to alter source wording to pass validation.
findings.validation_reason: At e443587 on Node v20.19.1 with a supported synthetic OpenAI image provider and an authorized in-memory staff store, faithfully labelled visible text containing 'הוא מרגיש שמחה.' plus an objective tree description caused both the actual extractor and singleExtract handler to return AI_OUTPUT_INVALID/422 after two calls, while ordinary transcription preserved the identical text, proving that the newly added combined-text guard at communication-ai.mjs:231 violates the verbatim-text and preserved poem/image contract at :224 and plan R8; live provider incidence was not measured.

actionable_findings.title: Image material guard rejects faithful quotations about emotions
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: A readable image containing text such as 'הוא מרגיש שמחה.' cannot be accepted as single-mode material even when the model transcribes that text exactly. The new attribution guard scans the combined verbatim source text and visual description, so it treats a quotation in a poem or message as an invented emotional claim, retries, and returns AI_OUTPUT_INVALID. This obstructs the preserved poem/image use case and can encourage the repair response to alter source wording to pass validation.
actionable_findings.validation_reason: At e443587 on Node v20.19.1 with a supported synthetic OpenAI image provider and an authorized in-memory staff store, faithfully labelled visible text containing 'הוא מרגיש שמחה.' plus an objective tree description caused both the actual extractor and singleExtract handler to return AI_OUTPUT_INVALID/422 after two calls, while ordinary transcription preserved the identical text, proving that the newly added combined-text guard at communication-ai.mjs:231 violates the verbatim-text and preserved poem/image contract at :224 and plan R8; live provider incidence was not measured.
